Overview: The Albin 32+2 Command Bridge is a large modified-V cruiser whose model name understates its roughly 36-foot-9-inch overall length. It combines a command bridge, wide side decks, protected running gear, cruising accommodations and single- or twin-diesel options. The design evolved from an early Sportfisher identity into a more cruising-oriented 32+2 with major layout and deckhouse updates in the mid-1990s.

ModelCharacter: A low-profile command-bridge cruiser that blends sportfishing cockpit utility with trawler-like fuel economy and a full-length prop-protecting keel. Its unusual step-up bridge provides excellent visibility without the ladder climb of a conventional flybridge.
DesignLineage: The model was introduced in 1989 as the Albin 32 Sportfisher.
In 1997 the same production family was renamed the Albin 32+2 Command Bridge; B-Atlas consolidates both names into this canonical record.
The deckhouse and bridge were updated in 1995, and an integral swim platform arrived around the 1997 renaming.
The later Albin 35 Command Bridge was a stretched development of the 32+2 concept.
OwnershipCharacter: Unusually spacious and accessible for a single-diesel boat, with wide side decks and good engine access. V-drive maintenance, bridge systems and optional twin-engine installations create more variability than on the smaller Albins.

ModelCharacter: A Finnish deep-V all-weather pilothouse designed around genuinely secure walkaround access, three exterior doors and high-speed offshore operation. It combines commercial-boat circulation with real two-cabin cruising accommodation and up to 45-knot performance.
DesignLineage: The 31+ is the modern successor-generation identity to earlier Nord Star 31 models and should not be collapsed into them without year-specific evidence.

ModelCharacter: A distinctive Sea Ray flush-deck motor yacht that places the helm and sheltered aft deck on one social level rather than separating the skipper on a flybridge. Beneath that unconventional profile is a high-volume two-stateroom planing yacht capable of roughly 18–22-knot cruise with gasoline or diesel inboards.
DesignLineage: Sea Ray introduced the 390 Motor Yacht for 2003.
The same model was renamed 40 Motor Yacht for 2006–2007 without becoming a fundamentally different hull.
The defining design departure is the single-level helm/aft-deck social area under a long hardtop rather than a conventional raised flybridge.
The 390/40 MY is distinct from Sea Ray's Sundancer express and Sedan Bridge families despite overlapping size.
OwnershipCharacter: Very comfortable and weather-protected, but this is a systems-dense motor yacht with twin mains, generator, HVAC, two heads and high air draft. Gas versions have high fuel burn; diesel versions cost more to maintain but suit heavier cruising better.

ModelVariations.Name: Seamaster
ModelVariations.Description: Fishing-oriented deck plan with maximum cockpit area; later examples could be fitted with an optional flybridge.

ModelVariations.Name: Navigator
ModelVariations.Description: Longer-house cruiser layout with enclosed head.

ModelVariations.Name: Pilot
ModelVariations.Description: Raised-pilothouse layout with additional overnight berth capacity.

ModelCharacter: Sea Sport's long-running 8'6"-beam flagship family introduced in 1985, built on one rugged 27-foot hull but offered as Seamaster, Navigator and raised-pilothouse Pilot deck plans. All prioritize fishing-capable cockpit space and rough-water Pacific Northwest utility, with the Pilot and Navigator adding substantially more cruising accommodation.
DesignLineage: The Sea Sport 27 was introduced in 1985 as an expansion of the company's 22- and 24-foot ranges.
The 27 Seamaster, Navigator and Pilot share the same basic hull but use different deckhouse and interior arrangements.
The Navigator lengthens the cabin and adds an enclosed head; the Pilot raises the helm and adds a Pullman-style berth.
Because these configurations share one hull and closely related systems, B-Atlas keeps them as one canonical 27 family with variant aliases rather than three duplicate models.
OwnershipCharacter: A strong all-weather boat with durable construction and unusually good owner loyalty. Many older examples use sterndrives and have been heavily customized or repowered; drive condition, transom/core moisture and propulsion configuration should be central to survey.
